name: Quit smoking
lead: Quitting smoking is a health practice that appearance communities also raise, mainly in connection with under-eye darkness and skin condition. Medical sources document the benefits of cessation for heart disease, cancer and lifespan.[1][2]
Cessation research is about disease and mortality. The reference material cited here does not address dark circles or facial appearance, so the appearance claim rests on community belief.
infobox: Improves dark circles and skin (untested here)

sections.h: Health effects of smoking and cessation
paras: A US cohort analysis of 113,752 women and 88,496 men found large hazards from smoking and benefits from quitting at various ages.[1] Reference sources describe smoking as a leading cause of preventable death, linked to heart disease, stroke, COPD and many cancers, and note that risk declines gradually after quitting, with heart-disease risk about half that of continuing smokers after one year.[2]
Smoking reduces blood supply and is described as able to worsen conditions such as eczema.[2] The sources reviewed do not specifically examine smoking and periorbital darkness.
CDC surveillance reports state that counselling and seven FDA-approved medications increase quit rates.[3] A national cohort reported weight gain after cessation, a concern some people cite.[4]
No studies found on quitting smoking and under-eye appearance. Large studies of cessation address mortality, disease and quit rates.[1][3]

lore.intro: Smoking is cited in appearance discussion as a factor that worsens dark circles and skin.

claims.claim: Smoking worsens dark circles and quitting improves them
claims.believers: Proponents say smoking harms circulation and skin, so stopping lets the under-eye area recover.
claims.experts: Reference sources document circulation and skin-condition effects of smoking; the reviewed sources do not specifically test periorbital darkness.[2]

card.summary: Quitting smoking is well supported for health; its effect on dark circles is untested.
card.note: Health benefits are documented; appearance benefit is not directly studied.

quick.overview:
Quitting smoking has well-documented health benefits. Appearance communities add that it may help skin and dark circles.

The cessation research cited here covers disease and mortality, not under-eye appearance.
quick.mechanism: Smoking reduces circulation and affects skin; stopping lets risk and some functions gradually improve.
quick.risks: Withdrawal can be distressing at first and some weight gain is reported after quitting. Clinicians and health agencies offer cessation support and approved medications.
